subtasks.title: Anchorless matcher, ambient fallback, tier slot, RankedMatch.tier diagnostic
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Read plan/004_24ebf0115d16/architecture/system_context.md (rankMatches control flow with verified line numbers, exported TIER* constants, comparator) and tier0_design.md §1–§2 BEFORE coding. Key verified facts: rankMatches (src/core/query.ts:352–431) enters the store at the first-char bucket via prefixRange(bucket) then sortedKeysSnapshot().slice(start,end); the admission gate is strict `m.score < threshold` discard (== survives); zero-result returns plain []; the internal RankedSortRecord.tier is already `number` and the comparator `b.tier - a.tier` sorts 0 below 1 UNCHANGED; the ONLY existing `tier: 0` is the zero-fragment ('#'-alone) listing sentinel (mutually exclusive with the match path — pin with a comment, do not let the dual meaning silently bite). MatchResult.tier union `1|2|3` (query.ts ~:122) must widen to `0|1|2|3`. clampScore exists. Score arithmetic sanity: 'query' in 'src/core/query.ts' → runStart 9, len 17 → 85−40·(9/17) = 63.8 → Math.round → 64; 'esk' in 'zendesk' → runStart 2, len 7 → 74; default-60 pass band runStart/len ≤ 0.625.
2. INPUT: No subtask inputs — this is the leaf. Available surface: matchFragment(f,c), exported TIER3_SCORE/TIER2_BASE_SCORE/TIER2_SKIP_FACTOR/TIER1_* constants, DEFAULT_FUZZ_THRESHOLD=60, RankOptions{limit?,fuzzThreshold?}, compareRankedMatches, RankedSortRecord, RankedMatch (src/core/types.ts:164, exactly 5 fields today — PINNED by test/query.test.ts:191 which you must update), and the CandidateStore API (prefixRange('') → [0,n) for the full-store pass; call prefixRange BEFORE sortedKeysSnapshot per the module's ordering invariant; store.get(k) undefined-check skips evicted ghosts).
3. LOGIC: Implement spec §04 h2.28 tier-0 (AMBIENT mode only — the `#` loose-mode entry is P1.M1.T2.S2): when lower !== '' AND the anchored loop admitted ZERO records AND fragment.length >= 3, run ONE anchorless pass over the full store — per key runStart = key.indexOf(lower); skip when -1; score = clampScore(Math.round(TIER0_BASE_SCORE − TIER0_SKIP_FACTOR·runStart/len(key))); strict score < threshold discard; record tier 0. Export NEW dedicated constants TIER0_BASE_SCORE=85 / TIER0_SKIP_FACTOR=40 (distinct semantics from TIER2 — runStart counts from 0, no anchor consumed; never inline literals). runStart=0 cannot admit in ambient mode (a position-0 run implies an anchored tier-3 match at 100, so recs would not be empty) — plain indexOf is the operative arm. Plural pruning + limit slice run after the fallback fills recs (existing machinery unchanged). Add `tier?: 0|1|2|3` OPTIONAL diagnostic to RankedMatch (types.ts): populated ONLY on the match path (anchored 1–3, anchorless 0); OMITTED by zero-fragment listing items (so `tier === 0` unambiguously means anchorless match — accepting a '#'-alone listing item must keep arming chains as today) — see system_context.md §Chain-arm reality. Rewrite the 'deliberately NOT on RankedMatch' JSDoc and the zero-fragment tier-0 sentinel comment. Copy tier into the public record where recs are mapped (today the map strips it). TDD pins in test/query.test.ts (compute expected scores from the exported constants — single-sourced, existing convention): esk→zendesk (74); query→src/core/query.ts (64); floor 3 (1–2-char fragments never fire tier-0 even on zero anchored results); a NON-EMPTY anchored result is byte-identical to pre-tier-0 output (fallback only rescues menus that would not appear); comparator rows 3>2>1>0; late runs gate at default 60; result-shape pin updated to the new field (present on match-path results, absent on '#'-alone listing items); MatchResult union consumers typecheck (npm run check). No mocking — pure core module over an in-memory CandidateStore constructed exactly as existing query.test.ts fixtures do.
4. OUTPUT: rankMatches with ambient tier-0 behavior; exported TIER0_BASE_SCORE/TIER0_SKIP_FACTOR; MatchResult tier union widened; RankedMatch.tier diagnostic — consumed by P1.M1.T1.S2 (perf gate times the new pass) and P1.M1.T2.S2 (loose-mode entry flips the precondition to always-consulted; chain-arm suppression reads tier === 0).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the tier-0 matcher + the exported TIER0 constants (calibration-starting-points pattern, same as TIER1/2/3), the rewritten RankedMatch/strip-site comments in query.ts, and the RankedMatch field doc in src/core/types.ts — all ride WITH this work; no separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Perf-gate row: tier-0 full-store pass < 3 ms p99 (CI at 3×)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Read plan/004_24ebf0115d16/architecture/tier0_design.md §6 and external_deps.md. test/perf-gates.test.ts gate pattern (verified, gate a at :76–121): makeStore(STORE_CAP) synthetic fixture (bench-fixtures.ts, seed 42, ~726–913 keys/bucket at 20k), 100-iteration warmup, 1000 timed performance.now() samples, p99 = dts[Math.ceil(0.99·N)−1], console.log actuals, expect(p99).toBeLessThan(3×budget) per the spec §09 CI rule. Gate a3 (zero-fragment full-store listing, loose <25 ms tripwire over 200 samples) is the full-store-pass precedent. `npm run bench` (test/bench/core.bench.ts, tinybench) is REPORTING-ONLY — pins live exclusively in perf-gates assertions.
2. INPUT: P1.M1.T1.S1's rankMatches with the ambient tier-0 fallback (the pass you are gating) and its exported TIER0 constants.
3. LOGIC: Add the new gate row per spec §09 h2.58: 'Tier-0 anchorless fallback full-store pass (fires only on empty anchored result; also # loose-mode scans) — < 3 ms p99' → CI assert expect(p99).toBeLessThan(9) over the 20k store, mirroring gate a's structure (warmup, 1000 samples, p99, console.log actuals). FIXTURE CAVEAT (load-bearing): synthetic keys are random-letter; you must PROBE at setup for a fragment (≥3 chars) whose ANCHORED result is EMPTY but whose anchorless indexOf hits ≥1 key — assert both sanity conditions in-test (the gate-a `range > 500` assertion is the precedent style) so the fallback demonstrably fires and the measurement is honest (includes the sort of the rescued set). Extend test/bench/core.bench.ts with a matching bench case only if it hosts comparable captured numbers (reporting-only). No mocking — synthetic fixtures ONLY; the shipped dictionary artifact is never loaded (existing suite contract).
4. OUTPUT: the passing gate row in test/perf-gates.test.ts + logged measured actuals — the gate numbers P1.M2.T1.S2 records in docs/M1-DoD.md (Budget | Measured | vs budget | CI bound (3×) | Verdict table row).

subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Read plan/004_24ebf0115d16/architecture/system_context.md §Config seam and tier0_design.md §4. Verified: HapaxConfig.fuzzThreshold is a REQUIRED number (src/pi/config.ts:73); DEFAULT_CONFIG bakes 60 at :101 (imported DEFAULT_FUZZ_THRESHOLD from src/core/query.ts — the rejectCommonness pattern); applyLayer's merge block (:261–271) writes clampNumber(v,0,100) (silent round-then-clamp; wrong type repairs with exactly one warning); loadConfig (:348–367) layers ~/.pi/agent/hapax.json then trusted .pi/hapax.json, later wins. Today explicit-set is INDISTINGUISHABLE from default — the exact gap. Spec §08 h2.52 already documents per-mode defaults (60 ambient / 45 trigger / explicit overrides both) — the schema row text is already correct; you add NO new user-facing config key (h2.53 'Not configurable' list stays untouched; tier boundaries remain semantics).
2. INPUT: The existing config surface above + query.ts's exported DEFAULT_FUZZ_THRESHOLD (60), post-P1.M1.T1.S1 (same file, additive edit — TIER0 constants already landed).
3. LOGIC: (a) Export the trigger-mode default constant from src/core/query.ts beside DEFAULT_FUZZ_THRESHOLD (e.g. TRIGGER_FUZZ_THRESHOLD = 45, JSDoc'd as the `#`-mode calibration default). (b) Expose explicit-vs-default from the config layer — implementation's choice per the PRD, both vetted: optional `fuzzThreshold?: number` (absent = unset; matches the established 'absent = DEFAULT' convention at query.ts's `opts.fuzzThreshold ?? DEFAULT`) OR keep the required number plus an internal set-flag set in applyLayer only when the key is present-and-valid. Constraint: the signal must NOT be a user-facing schema key. (c) ONE shared resolver — e.g. resolveFuzzThreshold(config, mode) → explicit ?? (mode === 'trigger' ? TRIGGER_FUZZ_THRESHOLD : DEFAULT_FUZZ_THRESHOLD) — exported where provider AND widget can both consume it (config.ts or query.ts; single source, no divergence). (d) TDD in test/config.test.ts extending the existing describe (:351 'fuzzThreshold — clamp in range, repair on type'): round-trip explicit value → resolves for BOTH modes; unset → 60 ambient / 45 trigger; clamp cases (−5→0, 150→100, 100.7→100, 60.4→60) preserve per-mode resolution; wrong-type repair → falls back to per-mode defaults with exactly one warning. Use the existing writeUserConfig + loadConfig(loadOpts()) harness with injected notify — no mocking beyond that.
4. OUTPUT: the exported resolver + explicitness signal + TRIGGER_FUZZ_THRESHOLD constant, consumed by P1.M1.T2.S2 at both display call sites; config.test.ts green.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] config.ts JSDoc on fuzzThreshold documenting the per-mode default semantics (explicit overrides both; unset → 60/45) + the new constant's JSDoc in query.ts — rides WITH the work; no separate docs subtask.

subtasks.title: Provider + widget loose-mode wiring, tier-0 always consulted, chain-arm suppression
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Read plan/004_24ebf0115d16/architecture/system_context.md (§Display paths, §Chain-arm reality — SCOUT-CORRECTED, trust it over the PRD's assumption) and tier0_design.md §3–§5. Verified facts: extractMatchState (src/pi/provider.ts:67–100) ALREADY returns the mode union {mode:'trigger',fragment,prefix} | {mode:'threshold',...}; the provider call site :599–603 passes flat config.fuzzThreshold with state.mode in scope; the widget default query closure (:436–440) takes ONLY a fragment — but createVisibilityMachine calls extractMatchState at :588 and already branches on mode (:617/:627/:701), so mode is available where the query runs. CRITICAL CORRECTIONS: (i) the widget Tab site NEVER arms a chain — WidgetOpts.chain (widget.ts:122–124) is wired by index.ts but read by NO widget code; chain.arm exists ONLY in provider applyCompletion (:644–686). 'Suppression at both Tab sites' is therefore: WIRE the provider site; PIN the widget site (comment + test asserting widget Tab acceptance never arms — do NOT invent widget arming). (ii) liveKeyByValue stores ONLY the key string (Map<value→key>) — tier is unreachable there today; look the accepted item up in lastLive.matches (≤8) or extend the map value. (iii) Chain-shim entries are FABRICATED RankedMatches (publishChain ~:455–470) — they must keep arming (their successors passed the anchored membership gate); the optional-tier design from T1.S1 (shims omit tier; check is strict `tier === 0`) preserves this. (iv) The chain MEMBERSHIP gate (armed-branch matchFragment filter, ~:540–560) is already anchored — NO change.
2. INPUT: P1.M1.T1.S1 — the anchorless pass inside rankMatches + RankedMatch.tier diagnostic (0 = anchorless match). P1.M1.T2.S1 — resolveFuzzThreshold(config, mode) + TRIGGER_FUZZ_THRESHOLD (45).
3. LOGIC: (a) Add the loose-mode entry to RankOptions in src/core/query.ts (e.g. loose?: boolean or mode — implementer's choice, JSDoc'd): when set, the tier-0 pass runs UNCONDITIONALLY (no zero-result precondition; floor 3 still applies) and its records are deduped against anchored admissions (skip keys already in recs — a key like 'queue' under '#que' matches tier-3 AND indexOf=0; anchored record wins). Implement the dedup skip unconditionally (vacuous in ambient mode) so one code path serves both. (b) Provider (provider.ts :599–603): resolve threshold via the shared helper from state.mode; pass the loose flag when mode === 'trigger'. Ambient word mode unchanged (60 default, zero-result precondition). (c) Widget (widget.ts :436–440 + :588): thread mode into the query seam (change the deps.query closure signature to (fragment, mode) or resolve inside the machine where extractMatchState already ran) with the SAME helper — no divergence. (d) Chain-arm suppression: in applyCompletion's plain-key (non-CHAIN_KEY_PREFIX) arm branch, skip chain.arm when the accepted item's RankedMatch.tier === 0; CHAIN_KEY_PREFIX branch untouched. Add the widget no-arm pin. (e) TDD suites: test/query.test.ts `#`-mode bullet (spec §09: '#query' → src/core/query.ts unconditionally; '#cfg' → tier-1 config_manager_service admits at 45 — tier-1 max 50, only strongest scattered survive; explicit fuzzThreshold overrides both mode defaults; dedup: anchored result for the same key is not duplicated by the anchorless pass); test/provider-match.test.ts (mode-aware threshold/loose pass-through); test/widget-visibility.test.ts (mode-threaded query; rm() fixtures unaffected by the optional field); test/chain.test.ts + chaining-gating.test.ts via the armViaTab helper (:202–218): tier-0 acceptance does NOT arm; anchored (tier 1–3) and chain-shim acceptance still arm; '#'-alone listing acceptance still arms (tier omitted). Mocking: none external exists — widget tests stub deps.query + fakeEditor() per the existing suite; provider/chain tests use the existing session-fixture harness.
4. OUTPUT: end-to-end loose mode on BOTH display paths with the explicit-override semantics, arming suppression live at the real arm site, all four suites green — the user-visible behavior P1.M2.T1 documents.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] JSDoc on the new RankOptions loose flag (semantics: tier-0 always consulted, deduped, floor 3) + call-site comments at provider.ts:599–603 and widget.ts:436–440 naming the per-mode resolution — ride WITH the work.
